extracted.intended_audience: journalists, journalism students, and general readers interested in news genres
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and defining characteristics for explanatory (explanatory reporting) journalism: reporting that presents ongoing news stories with greater context and pedagogical clarity so lay audiences can understand complex events or processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide greater context than traditional news sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanatory journalism or explanatory reporting "attempts to present ongoing news stories in a more accessible manner by providing greater context than would be presented in traditional news sources."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize background, trends, and causal context so readers grasp why a story matters beyond the immediate facts. The Wikipedia article associates this approach with outlets such as Vox, The Upshot, Bloomberg Quicktake, The Conversation, and FiveThirtyEight and notes that explanatory reporting has its own Pulitzer Prize category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present complicated events or processes in a comprehensible narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should "explain a complicated event or process in a comprehensible narrative."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shape reporting into a clear, narrative form that makes complexity intelligible to non-experts — not merely listing facts but organizing them into an explanatory storyline that reveals causes, consequences, and connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use intelligence and pedagogical flair
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanatory reporting "require[s] intelligence and a kind of pedagogical flair," linking understanding with the ability to teach a broad public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should combine subject-matter understanding with teaching skills: choose clear metaphors, analogies, definitions, and structures that help readers learn. The emphasis is on transmission of understanding, not just presentation of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make complex information accessible to a broad public
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanatory journalism aims to present news "in a more accessible manner" and to transmit understanding "to a broad public."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize clarity, avoid unnecessary jargon, and provide necessary background so non-specialist audiences can follow significance and implications. Accessibility is both stylistic (clear prose) and structural (context, timelines, Q&A, charts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve democratic information needs
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Michael Schudson, explanatory journalists "aid democracy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame explanatory work as contributing to informed public decision-making: explain stakes, trade-offs, and how events affect citizens, thereby supporting civic understanding and debate.
